meta.focus_timing: cost is days/10; 35/50/60 days. MD generic reference often uses cost8.6. Cyprus pacing remains to be playtested.
meta.progression: Shared sector roots are parallel from start; party routes require the specific governing subparty, formation and date conditions. Completed one-time focuses never reset on elections.
meta.layout: Shared roots x6/26/46/66; Turkish Cypriot community root x86; six political/economic roots x114/136/158/180/202/224. The research-led road-to-war root sits x6,y14; recovery x26,y20. All sections share one MD coordinate space.
meta.caps: Small-country balance targets: combined shared + ONE active political/economic programme research <=10%, organisation <=18%, generic+specific construction <=25%, office tax income <=35%. These are authored reward ceilings, not GDP increases. No free research slots or whole industrial sectors; strong modifiers remain constrained by actual capacity/workforce and political tradeoffs.
meta.economy: Costs use GDP-scaled modify_treasury_effect. Costs below are project grants/administration, not an assertion that 3%GDP purchases a factory. Construction queues and upkeep remain payable. Require funds on start AND completion; apply atomic debit/reward, or cancel with no reward. No double charging internal helpers.
meta.history: States145+146 are CYP in1970; state812 is ENG. The two-province MD map cannot represent the distribution of pre-1974 enclaves. Do not use resistance/compliance as a fake communal mechanic in core territory.
meta.party_lifecycle: Exact governing subparty gate, never just outlook. Six major routes: indices1,2,3,4,20 and combined21/22. Minor parties retain the shared national economy/military/diplomacy/community content. Persistent reveal preserves history; only the current government's political AND economic programme is enabled, avoiding election stacking. Shared funded projects and historical consequences persist. A global highest-milestone ledger caps all party reform credit at10; do not reset on elections.
meta.crisis: Historical mode favours the conditional1970-74 chain; successful talks/reform can avert it. EOKAB from1971, Grivas death1974, DIKO/DISY from1976, Makarios death1977 and CMP1981 need dated or explicitly alternate outcomes. Full chronology/portraits need implementation verification.
meta.cumulative_status: Numeric design audited statically against local keys. No engine run or multiplayer balance claim.

sections.title: The Republic and the Cyprus Question
sections.description: Negotiation, security and constitutional outcomes. Both communities have political agency; foreign players can accept or reject proposals.

sections.title: An Island Economy
sections.description: Choose the structure of development: tourism or productive diversification; credit openness or domestic control. No giant free industrial base.

sections.title: Defending a Small Republic
sections.description: A credible defensive force, external supply choices and civilian authority. Cyprus cannot win a symmetrical arms race with Turkey.

sections.title: Between the Guarantors and the Blocs
sections.description: Non-alignment, patron dependence and the Sovereign Base Areas. Offers are bilateral; another player's acceptance is never assumed.

sections.title: Crisis, Partition and Recovery
sections.description: Conditional historical crisis branch. The 1974 coup/invasion can happen, be averted or diverge; no inevitable date-triggered partition.

sections.title: Makarios: An Independent Developmental Republic
sections.description: Cooperative rural development or nationally controlled tourism, then external non-aligned credit versus domestic savings. Political concessions to patrons remain real.

sections.title: Clerides: A Commercial and Constitutional Republic
sections.description: Services and shipping versus export workshops; international capital versus a domestic lender. Office-income bonuses require actual staffed offices and are not GDP bonuses.

sections.title: EDEK: A Democratic Social Republic
sections.description: Funded public works or worker cooperatives; a tax-backed development fund or an actual loan with debt and repayment. Additional services have visible fiscal cost.

sections.title: AKEL: Labour, Industry and Independence
sections.description: Public food processing and repair industry versus worker-managed cooperatives; Eastern credit versus domestic funding. No heavy-industrial great power or free factories.

sections.title: The Progressive Front: A Civilian Enosis Mandate
sections.description: A genuinely civilian nationalist alternative: local enterprise or Greek integration, then open tenders versus patronage. Enosis remains contingent on negotiation or a separately chosen confrontation.

sections.title: The Enosis Coup and Security Regime
sections.description: A hardline regime can preserve civilian supply or divert capacity to readiness; taxes versus foreign dependence. Violence and expulsion retain separate lasting consequences, never economic rewards.

sections.title: The Turkish Cypriot Community
sections.description: Fazil Kucuk, Rauf Denktas, civilian organisations and the emerging CTP are distinct interlocutors. Address enclaves, restrictions, separate administration and political equality; they are not an obedient faction of the CYP ruling party.

sections.title: The Road to the Cyprus War
sections.description: A broken constitutional partnership is the background; Greek military influence, armed opposition and the1974 coup are distinct escalation mechanisms. Turkey and other players choose their own responses. Peace is possible.

starting_spirits.title: A Constitution in Abeyance
starting_spirits.note: Institutional breakdown since 1963; not an intrinsic ethnic penalty. Negotiation and an implemented constitutional agreement can resolve it.

starting_spirits.title: A Divided Chain of Command
starting_spirits.note: National Guard, police, armed organisations and foreign officers have competing loyalties.

starting_spirits.title: A Narrow Island Economy
starting_spirits.note: Small domestic market and import dependence; avoid pretending that Cyprus was economically stagnant.

starting_spirits.title: Independence under Guarantee
starting_spirits.note: Greece, Turkey and Britain constrain freedom of action; legal guarantee is not a universal defence pact.

starting_spirits.title: The Archbishop-President
starting_spirits.note: Leader-bound; removed on Makarios leaving office, dying or being overthrown. Conservative outlook is the existing game mapping, not a claim that he was Atlanticist.

starting_spirits.title: Fragmented Markets and Unsettled Access
starting_spirits.note: Legacy displacement, disrupted local economic links and uneven reciprocal access, not a blanket 1964-style blockade in 1970. Enclaves existed across the island. Together with the national narrow-economy penalty: -10% construction before other effects.

starting_spirits.title: Enclave Economies and Uneven Normalisation
starting_spirits.note: Coarse proxy for separate economic development, displacement and fragmented institutions, affecting all residents of the map state. Travel had substantially normalised by 1969. Combined construction -17%; positive growth 15% slower, not 15% GDP loss. No pre-existing NCY.

starting_spirits.title: Turkish Cypriot Enclaves and Separate Administration
starting_spirits.note: Separate communal institutions, displaced communities, uneven reciprocal access and duplicated services impose administrative/security costs. A 1969 UN report records largely restored Turkish Cypriot movement outside military areas; this is not an unchanged 1964 siege. Agreed services and remaining-access normalisation reduce the penalties.

starting_spirits.title: Displacement and Missing Persons
starting_spirits.note: Contingent on violence/war; NOT a January 1970 starting spirit. Separate from existing global refugee pressure to prevent duplicate costs.

starting_spirits.title: Shattered Communities
starting_spirits.note: Contingent destruction, flight and loss of trust; reconstruction can reduce this, coercion cannot simply erase it.

starting_spirits.title: The Armed Enosis Underground
starting_spirits.note: January 1970: the National Front and other armed opponents challenge Makarios. This is not EOKA B before its 1971 formation and is not a penalty for Greek Cypriot ethnicity. Civilian security reform, disarmament or an explicit regime change determine its later course.

community_design.context: Tied to conflict and administrative fragmentation, not ethnicity as an inherent penalty.

crisis_design.selected_phase_model: Current-map design: explicitly abstract the limited July foothold and negotiation phase without whole-state transfer or a pretend engine ceasefire. A later real engine offensive remains gated by actual force/readiness setup; final territory follows real results or accepted terms.
crisis_design.reaction_clock: Preparation focuses use their displayed duration. Reactive milestones are resolved by actor events/short decisions on the crisis clock, then recorded once using the real complete_national_focus effect. Never block the July20 response behind a35-day focus.
crisis_design.payload_rule: Each crisis instance has one outcome-applied ledger. The actor event owns costs and effects; focus completion only records the result. No invented reward=no parameter and no duplicate rewards or ultimata.
engine_limits: TUR and CYP1970 OOBs are deliberately empty; no functioning invasion is claimed.
States145 and146 each contain only one province; a July Kyrenia beachhead cannot be represented as control of all146.
NCY has cores on145/146/812; blind release risks the wrong territory.
Generic MD ceasefire/whitepeace may transfer ownership and impose720-day truce; use a bespoke tested adapter.
phase_rules: No war simply because Turkish Cypriots exist.
Coup pressure and communal tension are independent bounded tracks.
No compulsory1974 war if causes have been addressed; historical dates are conditional milestones.
The Turkish player retains its intervention decision; the CYP player retains its response.
No sovereignty transfer, mass population change or free modern units on the first-landing event.

event_contracts.constitutional_offer: Evaluate settlement progress, tension, both communities and their political representatives. Accepted offers unlock ratification, rejected offers preserve the current institutional penalties. One active conference instance only.
event_contracts.unitary_offer: Community representatives can refuse. No unilateral removal of constitutional breakdown. Failure adds 5 tension, not an automatic Turkish declaration of war.
event_contracts.federal_ratification: A dated or counterfactual federal compact requires consent from both communities; replace the old starting spirit with the agreed administrative programme. No transfer of state812.
event_contracts.shared_republic_ratification: A revised 1960-style central republic requires stronger settlement progress and both-community ratification; one settlement result flag, mutually exclusive with federation.
event_contracts.militia_disarmament: Supervised disarmament is negotiated across armed groups, not a blanket ethnic purge. Greek/other patrons may accept withdrawal or add coup pressure. No arbitrary free manpower.
event_contracts.reprisal_consequences: Abstract intimidation, killing, detention and forced displacement without operational detail. The focus applies tension+20 ONCE; the event adds displaced/missing-persons burden, affected-state destruction and the settlement block, without another tension debit. No population, GDP, core or military reward. Record perpetrating faction; apply the same harm rules to armed actors in either community.
event_contracts.crisis_conference: Offers to GRE/TUR/ENG plus local representatives. AI weighs actual regime, tension, claims and guarantees; human players decide. Refusal cannot force another player's action.
event_contracts.turkish_crisis_response: When a junta-backed coup succeeds, TUR chooses diplomatic ultimatum, bounded intervention or broader invasion; GRE chooses support/withdrawal/escalation; ENG chooses mediation/base defence; no forced player choices.
event_contracts.ceasefire_offer: All belligerents must accept a ceasefire; war control is retained until a settlement. NCY administration can emerge conditionally after intervention; recognition is a later separate question, with the 1983 declaration not misdated to 1974.
event_contracts.enosis_debate: Open a diplomatic/political dispute without annexation. A hardline majority mandate does not imply Turkish Cypriot consent. Peaceful Enosis needs a separate ratification chain; unilateral Enosis increases crisis risk.
event_contracts.enosis_ratification: Recheck GRE/CYP and both-community assent, guarantees, war state and ownership on resolution. State145/146 transfer only under agreed terms. Warn that independent CYP play ends; state812 stays ENG without separate British assent. Block permanent-independence capstone reciprocally.
event_contracts.base_cooperation_offer: ENG can accept/refuse; only accepted projects enable modifiers. A proposed subsidy must debit the donor and credit CYP with the same amount, checked against funds. Cooperation is not sovereignty transfer.
event_contracts.base_sovereignty_offer: Negotiated transfer of state812 requires explicit ENG acceptance and local settlement safeguards. British refusal gives no free annexation or automatic casus belli.
event_contracts.guarantee_conference: Greece, Turkey and Britain each retain a response; local community consent matters separately. Revise only the guarantees to which the parties actually agree.
event_contracts.missing_persons_cooperation: A civilian investigation/family-support initiative can begin early. The historical bicommunal CMP is 1981-gated, or deliberately marked early alternate institution; cooperation does not erase crimes.
